title: Guide
intro: You set everything up yourself. Steps tick themselves off as you go; the buttons take you to the right place. This guide is always here: Guide in the top bar, or F1.
allDone: Setup complete. Same path for new projects: pick a folder, assign a team, write the work to the lead.

provider.title: Choose an AI provider
provider.why: Agents think with a model. Here you decide which model runs, and with which account.
provider.how: Settings → Providers: Claude Code CLI (your own Claude account, the CLI on your computer), Codex CLI, an Anthropic or OpenAI API key, or the key-free Demo (for trying things out only; no real model is called). Pick a default; you can also give each agent a different provider/model.

org.title: Set up your organization and teams
org.why: Agents work in teams; you assign teams to a project and that team's agents work on it. A team can be used in several projects.
org.how: Organization → Chart: create nested company / department / team units. Quickest is Organization → Templates: a team plus agents in one click (e.g. Core Team, Software, Research, Marketing…). Everything from a template can be changed later.

agents.title: Add your agents
agents.why: The lead hands out work based on the agents' role, skills and job description; the clearer these are, the better the assignments.
agents.how: Organization → Agents → New agent: name, role, job description, skills, personality, look and (optionally) an agent-specific provider/model. Don't forget to add the agent to a team (agent page or Teams).

lead.title: Pick a lead
lead.why: The lead is the agent who talks to you in chat: it splits your request into tasks, assigns them to agents and reviews finished work.
lead.how: Choose the team's lead in Organization → Teams, or assign a project-specific lead in project settings. Without a lead the chat doesn't work; you can still create tasks yourself under Tasks.

perms.title: Review permissions
perms.why: Agents can touch real files, the terminal and servers. You choose what they're allowed to do; by default only reading is on.
perms.how: Settings → Permission Matrix: per-agent file read/write, terminal, network, browser and "ask for approval before every run". Server and database access is separate: Organization → Connections (default: no agent has access; changes in Production wait for your approval).

project.title: Give the project a folder and a team
project.why: Project = a folder + the teams working there. CLI agents only read and write files in the project folder. Even if the project is deleted, the folder and its contents stay on disk.
project.how: Double-click the project tab, or click the project name in the status bar → Project settings: folder, teams, lead, color. For a new project use + in the top bar, or Ctrl+P → "Open folder…".

work.title: Give the lead the first job
work.why: You describe the work; the lead splits it into tasks and hands them out to agents. Files you attach (PDF, Excel, Word, images…) are passed on to the tasks too.
work.how: Chat → #general: write what you want, where, and by when; attach files with the paperclip or drag and drop. To message a single agent directly, pick it from the list on the left. To add tasks by hand: Tasks → New task.

watch.title: Watch and steer
watch.why: You see live what the agents are doing and step in when needed; the lead reviews finished work, and you approve it or send it back.
watch.how: Terminal → Agent terminals: each agent's commands, tool calls and output; from the box below, Redirect (interrupts the current step) or Queue. Office shows the team on a map, Tasks manages tasks with drag and drop, Reports keeps reports and token usage, Decisions the decisions made. Pause all at the top keeps new tasks from starting and makes running agents wait at their next step (a command already running can finish; to end a run, stop it).

chat.name: Chat
chat.desc: Describe work to the lead (#general), talk to agents directly, read task threads. You can attach files.

office.name: Office
office.desc: The project's team in the pixel office: who's working, who's on a break, who's awaiting approval.

team.name: Team
team.desc: Agents working on the project, their teams, the lead and token usage.

terminal.name: Terminal
terminal.desc: Agent terminals (live stream + instruction box) and Shells (your own terminal in the project folder).

tasks.name: Tasks
tasks.desc: Kanban board: To do → In progress → In review → Done. Drag to start/stop.

reports.name: Reports
reports.desc: Task reports, the daily report and token / cost usage.

decisions.name: Decisions
decisions.desc: Decisions proposed by agents and the lead; accepted ones are written to memory.

files.name: Files
files.desc: Files you uploaded, files agents produced and changes in the project folder; preview, search, access.

chart.name: Chart
chart.desc: Company / department / team tree; add and move units, pick leads.

teams.name: Teams
teams.desc: Team members and leads; a team can be used in several projects.

agents.name: Agents
agents.desc: Add/edit agents: role, job description, skills, provider, permissions.

templates.name: Templates
templates.desc: Ready-made teams and companies (units + agents in one click).

skills.name: Skills
skills.desc: Instruction packages (SKILL.md) from GitHub, a folder, .zip or .md; assign them to agents or units.

apps.name: Apps
apps.desc: Connected apps (MCP): mail, design tools, databases…; per-tool approval and per-agent access.

connections.name: Connections
connections.desc: SSH servers and databases; per-agent access, Production approval, audit log.

permissions.name: Permission Matrix
permissions.desc: Per-agent file, terminal, network and browser permissions, plus connection permissions.

providers.name: Providers
providers.desc: Claude Code / Codex CLI, API keys, Demo; the default provider.

memory.name: Memory
memory.desc: What agents remember (per project and organization-wide).

data.name: Data management
data.desc: Usage, clean-up, log retention, backups and reset.

general.name: General
general.desc: Autopilot, lead review, project selection at startup.

feedback.name: Feedback
feedback.desc: A suggestion, a bug, a thank-you or a rating: tells you what to write and opens a mail to the developer.

coffee.name: Buy me a coffee
coffee.desc: Support the developer (opens in your browser).

places.security: Security: agents can only reach what you allow; file contents and server output are treated as data, not instructions; your secrets (keys, passwords) are never shown to agents.

shortcuts.sendInstruction: Send the instruction in an agent terminal
